source.title: Homogeneous Vector Capsules Enable Adaptive Gradient Descent in Convolutional Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizer settings and reports held-out classification accuracy. Its results qualify the claim: performance depends on architecture, dataset, capsule configuration, and optimizer settings; it does not report training error or a measured generalization gap.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, network width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected feature extractors, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its optimizer comparisons use test accuracy; descriptions of prior studies are not rows. The 60-row limit requires a selection from the optimizer tables; rows emphasize the fully connected output baselines and reported optimizer winners, plus representative capsule comparisons.
record.test_reason: The experiments compare Adam with RMSProp, which is also adaptive even when its adaptability is dampened by a large epsilon. No SGD or momentum-SGD comparator tests V4's optimizer contrast. Replacing a CNN's output layer with capsules also does not test V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected-network contrast. The authors discuss these claims, but their own results measure different comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the direction of the authors' interpretation but understates its strength: they claim HVCs enable adaptive optimization without a generalization gap and reduce the need for optimizer tuning. They report a 19.16% relative improvement in average simple-CNN accuracy, excluding three failed baseline runs, and an average 1.32% advantage for the best Inception capsule configuration over its baseline. Their experiments report classification accuracy without training-to-test gaps or SGD comparisons, so they do not establish the claimed elimination of an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization penalty.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the CNN output layer to homogeneous vector capsules and compares optimizer configurations; it does not use the original claim's random-label memorization procedure or measure a train-test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture/output configuration, optimizer and its epsilon/base learning-rate schedule; batch size differs for Food-101 because of hardware constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 6 and 7 compare Adam configurations with large-epsilon RMSProp configurations. For example, Food-101 S1 reaches 69.89% with O1, 54.98% with O3, and 68.64% with O4; Inception I1 reaches 82.52% with O2 and 84.03% with O3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out accuracy under Adam versus large-epsilon RMSProp depends on dataset, architecture, and optimizer configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing fully connected output layers with HVCs often improves classification accuracy, while retaining convolutional feature extractors. Food-101 Inception baselines outperform every HVC configuration under O1 and O2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: HVC output layers can improve CNN classification accuracy, with gains depending on architecture and optimizer configuration.

record.problems: No random-label condition, training accuracy, or direct generalization-gap measurement. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Reported accuracy comparisons are entangled with changes to the output architecture. The Food-101 S1/O2 run reached 0% accuracy, and two other S1/O2 runs did not exceed chance, complicating optimizer comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Additional optimizer-by-model-by-dataset values from Tables 6 and 7 are omitted due to the 60-row limit. Included the S1 baseline optimizer values across all three datasets, the reported best or representative HVC outcomes, and I1 baseline optimizer values across all three datasets; excluded remaining HVC configuration results not needed to capture stated optimizer and setting differences.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, local connectivity, learned sparsity, and transferred initialization. Both experimental backbone families are convolutional.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning; training-performance comparisons; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and language benchmarks.
Batch-size comparisons within a workload at fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Controlled dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All 44 accuracy values agree with the supplied tables. None warrants a verdict on V1–V8. The absence of training accuracy alone would not exclude V4, which names held-out performance; the missing SGD comparator is decisive. Large epsilon does not make RMSProp an SGD control. The record's existing V4 limits_scope label should be removed. O1/O2 schedules were transferred from ImageNet rather than tuned on each experimental dataset.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond that needed for zero training error and test error across width.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, SGD or momentum SGD comparisons, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models. Training performance and the training-to-test gap are not measured.
Large versus small batches at fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with weight decay or data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Simple monolithic CNN, Imagewoof and Food-101, and Inception v3 comparisons across the tested datasets
reader_labels.reason: Adaptive optimizer accuracy varies by setting: O4 is best for the simple CNN in the authors' account, while O3 is best in two Inception v3 dataset comparisons and O1 beats O3/O4 on the S1 Food-101 baseline; the baseline S1 also performs very poorly with O2. Rows R2, R16, R29-R32, R36-R44.
